I farm in Quzhou County, Hebei, so I will stay with the pattern I trust most on my land: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the safest way for me to use the full year, match the local weather, and keep grain coming from the same fields twice. I know these two crops, I can manage them with the machinery and labor I already have, and I do not want to take extra risk on unfamiliar cash crops. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is steady and suits my habit of managing for reliable yield. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because maize responds well to it and gives me stronger production in our area.

For wheat, I will keep fertilizer moderate and balanced. I will put on nitrogen as the main driver, add phosphorus to build roots and tillers, and use some potassium to hold the crop steady. I will irrigate several times if water allows, mainly at the key stages when the crop really needs it. I will watch weeds, aphids, rust, and other diseases, and I will spray only as needed, but in a normal year I expect a few pesticide applications. I will use rotary tillage where it fits my equipment and keeps work simple.

After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize so I do not lose soil moisture or the season. For maize I will put more nitrogen than wheat, with some phosphorus and potassium underneath. I will irrigate fewer times than wheat because the rainy season helps, but I will still water when the crop is under stress. I will control weeds early and then watch for armyworm, borers, and leaf disease. I will keep tillage light and practical. My goal is not fancy management. I will aim for a stable crop, controlled costs, and a full-year grain harvest from the land.
